chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Anbasa al-'Abid, who said:

A man came and complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about his relatives. So he (the Imam) said to him: 'Suppress your anger and do (maintain relationships).' So he said, 'They are doing and doing (bad things).' So (the Imam) said: 'Do you want to become like them, so that Allah will not look at you?'

key_terms.فَلَا يَنْظُرَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ: So that Allah does not look at you (lose divine favor)

ai.seo_question: How should one respond to difficult relatives according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises a man complaining about his relatives' misconduct to practice 'akz al-ghayz' (suppressing anger) and maintain ties despite their actions. The Imam warns against reciprocal bad behavior, stating that if the man mirrors their conduct, Allah will not look upon him with favor, emphasizing that enduring kinship ties requires distinctiveness from the wrongdoers rather than imitation. This highlights the Shia emphasis on active patience (sabr) and moral superiority in preserving family bonds.
